original.target_description: Study 1, first randomized condition: incorrect choice of image A as having more people, by 2016 vote choice (Trump voters, Clinton voters, nonvoters), Results/Figure 2. The original uses vote choice, not Republican party identification. No separate pooled binary non-Trump contrast is printed.

n.location: p. 140 (PDF p. 6), Figure 2 caption; p. 139 exclusions
n.quote: N = 158 nonvoters, 275 Clinton voters, and 218 Trump voters.
n.sample_role: Respondents in the Figure 2 first-condition vote-choice analysis; three mutually exclusive final voter groups.
n.exclusions: Third-party voters excluded from analysis (p. 139); only the first randomized question condition is represented. No further Figure 2 exclusions specified.

es.quote:
Figure 2 shows the proportion of respondents who selected the incorrect photo
               (image A) as the one that had more people. Note that the rate of selecting
               that photograph among nonvoters (3 percent) and Clinton voters (2 percent) is
               negligible—essentially in line with what we would expect simply from meas-
               urement error. However, a much higher percentage of Trump voters—15 per-
               cent—selected image A as showing more people. A similar pattern is clear
               for Trump approval. The difference in selecting the incorrect photo based on
               one’s vote choice or approval of Trump is statistically significant (p < .01)

notes: Analytic N arithmetic: 158 nonvoters + 275 Clinton voters + 218 Trump voters = 651 respondents. This is the full printed vote-choice comparison, not a pairwise Trump-versus-Clinton N and not the approval analysis. Weighted incorrect-response percentages are printed separately as 3 percent nonvoters, 2 percent Clinton voters and 15 percent Trump voters. No scalar comparative effect or named test statistic is printed; percentages were not converted into an effect. The same paragraph reports p < .01 for vote-choice/approval differences; p is unassigned here. Approval is a separate moderator and is not substituted for voter groups. Only assigned unfinished original fields were examined for output; other fields and replication/success are unassigned placeholders.
